newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. says penalties on China textile exports remain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says penalties on China textile exports remain.

text.p: The United States will not scrap $19 million worth of penalties on imports of Chinese textiles, a U.S. negotiator said on Sunday.
Washington slapped the penalties on imports of Chinese textiles last September, saying Beijing was shipping textiles through third countries to evade quota restrictions.
"The transshipment charges that were made in September still stand as they did," senior U.S. textile negotiator Rita Hayes told a news conference.

China and the United States signed a four-year textile accord on Sunday after a marathon six days of talks. Beijing announced after the signing that it would call off retaliatory measures on selected U.S. imports.

China had threatened to retaliate against the U.S. penalties by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks, but had delayed such action to allow time for a compromise to be reached.
